report.verdict: alive, as specified (no rule change); but mana barely binds: Expert leaves 5.4 mana unspent a turn
report.numbers: Expert beats Random 98.8%, Greedy 95.5%, Racer 81.3% (400 games each, seats alternated); Expert equals Greedy in 15.1% of 52,255 decisions; first player wins 55.5% of 400 Expert mirror games; 0 games hit the turn cap; Expert passes all three set positions on 5 seeds each. Expert mirrors last 41 turns and end on three Keys in 45% of games, on a deck run out in 55%. Greedy and Racer mirrors end on a deck run out in 77-87% of games, and there the first player wins 67-72%, because the second player, who starts with one card more, runs out first.
loop: The game is denial against assembly: whoever plays a third Key gives the other one turn to break one. Hits ignore Guard and kill Key A or C in one card (Hit 3, Hit 5), so a player holding Hits can deny almost indefinitely, and Expert keeps its Hits for exactly that.

With nothing to gain, a player whom the deck-out order favours does nothing: in one traced Expert mirror the first player ended 18 turns in a row without a play, holding Hits, and broke each third Key as it landed. Expert plays 0.9 cards a turn.

Board units matter only as Key attackers and Guards; trades are worth taking only when a unit threatens a Key (the set position had to put a Key at stake for the free trade to change the result: with no Keys anywhere it changed nothing, 79.5% against 80.1% over 1,500 play-outs).
Fetch thins the deck, so it hastens your own deck run out; Expert often declines it when the deck order favours it.
report.cost: Mana barely binds: it is at its cap of 10 in 56% of turns, Expert ends 86.7% of turns with mana unspent (5.4 a turn) and empties its hand in 0.5%; a card is priced out in 36% of turns. What limits play is cards (one draw a turn) and the choice to hold Hits for denial, not cost.
report.expertNote: Expert: determinized flat Monte Carlo over single actions, 1,200 play-outs with successive halving, play-outs 14 turns deep (Greedy or Racer per side with a denial sense, 4% noise) then scored by Keys held, board, hand and deck.
